title: Content Identity V1 (examples and datasets)
description: Wire shapes for traigent.content_identity.v1: tenant-keyed, content-addressed example identity (example_id over the INPUT, example_version over id + expected output + metadata), and order-free MULTISET roots for datasets (dataset_root) and for what one trial actually evaluated (evaluated_root). Normative construction: docs/identity/content-identity-v1.md. Reference implementation: traigent_schema/example_identity.py. Conformance vectors every implementation MUST pass: traigent_schema/data/content_identity_v1_vectors.json. This is a new, additive contract: it does not change DatasetVersionV1.content_digest (datasets/dataset_version_schema.json), the fp2 dfp2o fingerprint, or any certification family contract. Every identifier here is fixed-width lowercase ASCII, so byte order, code-point order and UTF-16 code-unit order agree and every runtime sorts them identically. Integer counts are bounded by the jcs_v1 safe-integer ceiling (2**53 - 1). Every string pattern in this file ends with the portable end anchor (?![\s\S]) instead of $: in Python's re (which Python jsonschema uses) $ also matches before a trailing newline, so '^x$' would accept 'x\n' -- a second spelling of one identifier. (?![\s\S]) means end-of-string in both ECMA-262 and Python.

ContentIdentitySchemeV1.description: Scheme tag carried by every record so a later scheme can coexist without ambiguity.

ContentIdentityDomainRegistryV1.description: Closed registry of the v1 domain-separation strings. example_id and example_version are each BOTH the domain part of the HKDF-SHA-256 'info' that derives that purpose's key from the tenant master (info = UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || UTF8(tenant_id); salt = UTF8('traigent.content_identity.v1')) AND the HMAC message prefix UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || jcs_v1(payload). key_id is the domain part of an HKDF 'info' only (8-byte output). multiset_leaf, public_input, agent_build and evaluator_version are message prefixes of UNKEYED SHA-256 constructions (agent_build: agents/agent_version_manifest_v1_schema.json; evaluator_version: evaluation/evaluator_version_manifest_v1_schema.json).

KeyIdV1.description: Public key id of the tenant key version that minted an identifier: 'k' + hex(HKDF-Expand(PRK, UTF8('traigent.content_identity.key_id.v1') || 0x00 || UTF8(tenant_id), 8)). A different master or a different tenant_id gives a different kid, so ids minted under a rotated key, or for another tenant, are never confused. It reveals nothing about the key. NORMATIVE: the kid is the second colon-separated field of every ex1:/exv1:/msr1: identifier, and a consumer MUST check that it equals the record's key_id for the record, its root(s) and every member. kid is 64 bits and therefore only probabilistically unique: lookups are always tenant-scoped, and a kid collision among one tenant's key versions is a hard error at key creation (the Backend generates a new master).

ExampleIdV1.description: 'ex1:' + kid + ':' + lowercase hex HMAC-SHA-256(K_example_id, UTF8('traigent.content_identity.example_id.v1') || 0x00 || jcs_v1({input, context?})). Identifies the INPUT (with context when present): stable while the input is unchanged, whatever happens to the label. Tenant-scoped: the same input in two tenants yields unlinkable ids.

ExampleVersionV1.description: 'exv1:' + kid + ':' + lowercase hex HMAC-SHA-256(K_example_version, UTF8('traigent.content_identity.example_version.v1') || 0x00 || jcs_v1({example_id, expected?, metadata?})). Changes when the expected output or version-relevant metadata changes. Its kid MUST equal its example_id's kid.

MultisetRootV1.description: 'msr1:' + kid + ':' + lowercase hex RFC 9162 Merkle Tree Hash (SHA-256, 0x00 leaf / 0x01 node prefixes) over the multiset's leaves, sorted ascending by (example_id, example_version). Leaf data = UTF8('traigent.content_identity.multiset_leaf.v1') || 0x00 || jcs_v1([example_id, example_version, count]). Order-free; duplicates change the root through count. The tree itself is unkeyed (the leaves are already keyed tokens), so an inclusion proof verifies without any key. The empty multiset's root is SHA-256 of the empty string.

PublicInputDigestV1.description: OPT-IN, UNKEYED: 'exu1:' + lowercase hex SHA-256(UTF8('traigent.content_identity.public_input.v1') || 0x00 || jcs_v1({input, context?})). Anyone who can guess the input can confirm it, so producers MUST emit it only when the tenant opted in AND the example comes from a public benchmark. Its only purpose is contamination checks against public benchmark inputs across tenants.

Sha256HexV1.description: A lowercase hex SHA-256 value (an RFC 9162 audit-path node).

ExternalIdV1.description: Interop: the example's id in the system it came from (Phoenix external_id, Braintrust/LangSmith example id, MLflow dataset_record_id, Inspect Sample.id, Opik item id, Promptfoo testIdx, OpenAI datasource_item_id). Annotation only: NEVER part of example_id or example_version, and never used for identity.

SourceRefV1.description: Interop: where a dataset (or an example) was imported from, so a Traigent root can be mapped back to the source system's own version handle. Annotation only; never hashed.

platform.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was closed_enum; contract has no enum/const, so the value is not provably content-free
platform.description: Lowercase source platform name, e.g. langsmith, braintrust, phoenix, opik, mlflow, wandb, huggingface, dvc, inspect, promptfoo, openai_evals, file.

version.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was closed_enum; contract has no enum/const, so the value is not provably content-free
version.description: The source system's version handle as it names it (LangSmith as_of timestamp or tag, Braintrust _xact_id, Opik version_hash, Phoenix version id, W&B 'artifact:vN' or digest, Hugging Face revision SHA, DVC .dir md5, MLflow digest). null when the source has no version handle.

ExampleIdentityV1.description: The identity of one example. The (example_id, example_version) pair is the unit of paired comparison; example_id alone is the unit of overlap/leakage checks.

supersedes.description: Annotation only, never hashed: the example_id this example replaces (e.g. after a typo fix changed the input and therefore the id). Lets lineage survive input edits; it never changes example_id or example_version.

MultisetMemberV1.description: One leaf: a distinct (example_id, example_version) pair and how many times it occurs. count is dataset multiplicity only; evaluation repetitions/epochs are recorded separately on the trial and are NEVER folded into count.

MultisetMembersV1.description: The member list, sorted ascending by (example_id, example_version) with no repeated pair (repeats are merged into count). Producers MUST emit this canonical order; consumers MUST recompute the root from the members (and compare it with the stated root) rather than trust either the order or the stated root.

ConflictingExampleIdsV1.description: example_ids that occur with MORE THAN ONE example_version in this multiset (same input, different labels). The root is still defined; a non-empty list is a data-quality warning the product MUST surface, and paired comparisons MUST exclude these ids.

DatasetIdentityV1.description: The content identity of one dataset version: its multiset root plus the counts a relying party needs. distinct_count is the RFC 9162 tree size; an inclusion proof does not authenticate tree size by itself, so a relying party MUST take it from here (from the signed record), never from the proof. Exactly one of members / members_ref is present; consumers MUST recompute the root from the members. Only record_state='complete' is certifiable.

dataset_id.description: The Backend dataset (benchmark) this version belongs to, when it is registered. Identity of the NAME, not of the content.

distinct_count.description: Number of distinct (example_id, example_version) leaves: the Merkle tree size.

total_count.description: Sum of member counts: the number of rows including duplicates.

members_ref.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was opaque_ref; contract has no ref pattern, so the value is not provably content-free
members_ref.description: Opaque server reference to the stored member list when it is not inlined. Exactly one of members / members_ref (oneOf). Either way a consumer MUST obtain the list and recompute dataset_root from it.

EvaluatedSetV1.description: What ONE trial actually evaluated: the multiset of (example_id, example_version) it scored, as a root plus its member list (or a reference to where the list is stored). evaluated_root uses the same construction as dataset_root, so a trial that evaluated the whole dataset exactly once has evaluated_root == dataset_root. repetition is the trial-level repeat/epoch index and is never folded into member counts.

repetition.description: 0-based repeat/epoch index of this evaluation pass.

dataset_root.description: The dataset version this trial drew from.

members_ref.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was opaque_ref; contract has no ref pattern, so the value is not provably content-free
members_ref.description: Opaque server reference to a stored member list, when the list is not inlined. Exactly one of members / members_ref MUST be present (oneOf). Whichever is used, a consumer MUST fetch the list and recompute evaluated_root from it; the root is never trusted on its own.

InclusionProofV1.description: RFC 9162 section 2.1.3 inclusion proof that one member (exact pair AND count) is a leaf of a multiset root. Verification needs no key. tree_size MUST be checked against the signed record's distinct_count by the relying party: the proof alone does not authenticate it.

MemberListRefV1.x-content-note: INV-GAP: was closed_enum; contract has no enum/const, so the value is not provably content-free
MemberListRefV1.description: Reference to a member list stored by the Backend's member-list store (milestone M3): 'ml1:' + the store's id for the list. A tenant-scoped handle, not a digest: whoever resolves it MUST fetch the list and recompute the stated root from it. The value a producer puts in a members_ref field once the store exists; not yet emitted by either SDK (above the inline cap they withhold the slot instead, see execution/content_identity_wire_v1_schema.json).

RecordStateV1.description: draft: still being assembled, may lack linkage; never certifiable. complete: every field the certificate contract needs is present (see each record's if/then); only complete records are certifiable.
